The process for extending the loan period for a rare book in the Special Collections section involves making an appointment at least 2 working days ahead of time. The book can only be consulted in the reading room during the library's operating hours, Monday to Friday 09:00–17:00. Photography for personal study is permitted, but publication requires written permission from the special collections librarian.

Overdue standard items accrue fines of 30 pence per item per day, capped at £15 per item. Short-loan items (4-hour loans) accrue £1 per hour with no cap. Lost items are charged at the replacement cost plus a £10 administrative fee.

The procedure for requesting a special exhibition item from the library's collection involves making an appointment at least 2 working days ahead of time. The material can only be consulted in the reading room, and photography for personal study is permitted. Publication of any material requires written permission from the special collections librarian.

Overdue standard items accrue fines of 30 pence per item per day, capped at £15 per item. Short-loan items (4-hour loans) accrue £1 per hour with no cap.

Inter-library loans allow patrons to request items not held by Greystone, with a limit of 2 requests per patron per month free of charge, and an additional charge of £3 per request thereafter. The delivery time is typically 5–10 working days, and inter-library loans cannot be renewed. In contrast, special collections materials can only be accessed in the reading room during specific hours and days, and photography for personal study is permitted, but publication requires written permission from the special collections librarian.
A postgraduate student can borrow 4 more items compared to an undergraduate student.
The cost for 3 inter-library loan requests in total is £9. The first 2 requests are free, and each request thereafter costs £3.
